primitives.name: Tackle Over Formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: FORMATIONS AND DIAGRAMS OF PLAYS 215 Tackle Over Formation—Quarter Back Run.
primitives.assumptions: Center leads blocking chain to the left, guards break through gaps to cut off reinforcements, tackles block laterally, ends provide auxiliary support, and fullback mirrors the right halfback's interference pattern.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when defensive linemen collapse the interior gap before the center completes his lead block, creating a sack.

layer2.mapping: Maps formation geometry to a conformal prediction set for quarterback rushing yards, where the blocking hierarchy defines a convex hull around the ball carrier's trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Observed quarterback rushing yards within the convex hull formed by blocker positions.

primitives.name: Good Play Against Close Defense
primitives.verbatim_quote: A good play to use if the opponents are playing close on defense.
primitives.assumptions: The defensive front aligns tightly to compress running lanes, forcing the offensive line to execute precise gap control.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when defenders blitz from uncovered angles, overwhelming the established blocking assignments.

layer2.mapping: Replicates the strategic logic as a zero-sum game where the offense maximizes expected utility under adversarial uncertainty, while the defense minimizes it.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of the play against defensive alignments with average depth of 4.5 yards or less.

primitives.name: Open Up or Make Ground
primitives.verbatim_quote: It will open them up or the play will make ground.
primitives.assumptions: The offensive line achieves at least a 2-yard lateral separation from the defensive front, creating a viable running lane.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the defensive alignment collapses the created space within 0.4 seconds, negating the initial opening.

layer2.mapping: Translates the outcome into a binary classification problem: whether the quarterback gains at least 3 yards after contact, conditioned on the blocking efficiency metric.
layer2.telemetry: Binary indicator of positive yardage gained after the first contact point.

primitives.name: Follow Right Halfback Interference
primitives.verbatim_quote: FORMATIONS AND DIAGRAMS OF PLAYS 215 Tackle Over Formation—Quarter Back Run. A good play to use
primitives.assumptions: The fullback tracks the right halfback's movement vector to provide additional mass and depth to the primary blocking chain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when the fullback's angle deviates more than 15 degrees from the halfback's path, creating a blind side vulnerability.

layer2.mapping: Encapsulates the coordination as a derived kernel that augments the quarterback's effective forward momentum by adding the fullback's velocity component parallel to the line of scrimmage.
layer2.telemetry: Change in quarterback speed along the line of scrimmage when the fullback engages in interference.
